newsitem.title: USA: Brady debt prices recoup losses on Brazil, T-bond.
newsitem.headline: Brady debt prices recoup losses on Brazil, T-bond.

text.p: Emerging debt prices bounced back Wednesday from their massive slump, as Brady bonds soared amid strong impetus from U.S. stocks and bonds, and the market dismissed fears of currency turmoil in Brazil, traders said.
Bradies recovered fully from Tuesday's malaise, during which prices tumbled amid fears that recent Asian currency turmoil might affect the Brazilian real.

"A lot of people looked at the market nerviousness and decided that it was not well founded," said Joyce Chang, managing director at Merrill Lynch. "We just did not see the (Asian) contagion affecting Brazil."

U.S. analysts said Brazil deftly addressed any uncertainty by quickly reaffiming its excahnge-rate policy and stating that privatization revenues would be dedicated to reducing the public sector deficit.

"What really helped Brazil was when they announced that all the privatization proceeds would go towards deficit reduction," said Richard Segal, head of fixed-income research at Santander Investments. "It was just what the market needed at the right time."
Brady traders reported they saw prices lifted by inter-dealer activity and intermittent client flows.
Brazil's benchmark "C" bond stormed 1-5/8 higher to 82-1/2 bid, while Argentine FRBs picked up 1/2 to 94-1/4.
The gains were uneven, but most Brady bonds of the major Latin nations tightened 10-20 basis points.
The Brady bond rally was led by a stellar day on the U.S. Treasury market, as signs of tame inflationary pressures pushed the benchmark T-bond up 28/32 to yield 6.48 percent.
Also, Dow Industrials stormed to a record close at 8038.
Some traders expressed concern the Brady market so quickly cut its losses, given that the market had already been at historically tight levels before the uncertainty over Brazil.
"I think we're all concerned about how quickly we bounced back," Segal said. "If it had taken place without the U.S. (T-Bond) being up a point I would be more concerned."
But with the Brady market back to its levels from Monday, analysts said the market could continue to gain from global interest in high yield products.
Also Wednesday, Argentina announced it would delay the launch of a planned $750 million seven year global bond issue because of volitile markets.
